canonical_data: A SQLite database, or Postgres, holding agent records, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md and MEMORY.md files, sessions, users and API keys, plus skill folders on disk
current_repo_note: Covers the open FastClaw runtime and its bundled dashboard. The README names ChatClaw as an application built on top of it, and a hosted multi-tenant service is reserved to the licensor, so neither is reviewed here. Two bundled skill-creator folders carry their own Apache-2.0 licence file and are not part of the licence recorded here.
strengths: Identity, memory, sessions, and configuration live in a database the operator controls, and the identity and memory files are editable from the dashboard
The sandbox is a hard boundary on hosted deploys and an opt-in tool on self-hosted installs, with Docker and E2B backends and workspace sync after each tool call
An OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Agent Communication Protocol routes, MCP, and a JSON-RPC plugin system make it embeddable in another product
weaknesses: The licence is Apache 2.0 with added conditions that forbid operating a multi-tenant service for unrelated organizations and removing the interface branding, so it is source-available rather than open source
The repository was created in March 2026 and the changelog already records breaking changes, so operators should expect upgrade work
On a self-hosted install the host shell is the default and the model opts into the sandbox per call, so isolation is not the default
why_it_matters: A compact Go runtime for operators who want many always-on, channel-connected agents with durable identity and memory without adopting a Python agent stack.
